standard.title: Capitals in titles, commas in lists
standard.description: recognise that capital letters are used in titles and commas are used to separate items in lists
standard.prior_knowledge: Students understand sentence boundary punctuation and capital letters for proper nouns and sentence beginnings (AC9E1LA10). They have not yet recognised capital letters as a title-marking convention or commas as list separators.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can recognise that capital letters mark titles and that commas separate items in lists.

nodes.label: Capital letters in titles
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify capital letters used in the titles of texts and explain that this is a convention for marking titles, distinct from sentence-start capitals.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify capital letters in the title of a text and explain that titles are capitalised by convention.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and compare capital letter usage in titles across different text types — books, news articles, posters, headings — and discuss what counts as a title.
wider: Compare different capitalisation conventions in titles (all words vs content words only vs first word only) across different text types and contexts
Identify titles in digital contexts (website headings, video titles, app names) and compare capitalisation conventions with print texts

response_modes.reason: Students need to build accurate recognition of title capitalisation as a distinct convention from sentence-start capitals. Precision in distinguishing these two uses requires targeted practice — more examples across text types, with attention to what is and isn't capitalised in titles.

success_criteria: Student can identify capitals in a title and explain this as a title convention.
Student does not confuse title capitalisation with sentence-start capitalisation.

nodes.label: Commas in lists
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify commas used to separate items in a list and explain their function as separators.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify the commas in a sentence with a list of items and explain that they separate the items.
nodes.typical_width: Identify commas in lists across a variety of texts — shopping lists, class descriptions, informative texts — and discuss where commas appear vs where 'and' is used instead.
wider: Compare list punctuation with and without commas in different contexts and discuss how commas prevent ambiguity
Identify lists in multimodal texts (e.g. dot-point lists vs running-text lists) and compare how commas function in each

response_modes.reason: Accurate comma placement in lists is a precision skill. Students commonly omit the comma before 'and' or insert commas where they are not needed. Targeted practice — reading and producing lists — builds the fluency needed before this skill appears in writing.

success_criteria: Student can identify commas separating items in a list.
Student can explain that commas separate list items and that 'and' typically precedes the final item.
